name: Tire Rotation
summary: Second pass closed the TPMS question: NHTSA vPIC decodes this VIN as a 2010 BMW 328i sedan with TPMS 'Direct' (so metal-stem sensors; reset via iDrive or turn-signal stalk after rotation). Wheel bolt torque 120 Nm now has 6+ independent secondary sources (Autodoc x3 guides, Bolidenforum BMW-data table, FCP 119 Nm, ECS, Bimmerpost, Department 69 quoting TIS) so it is VERIFIED_SECONDARY, with one dissent (koleso.ee 115 Nm); no BMW owner's manual or TIS page could be read, so primary:false. Rotation pattern depends on the tire package: square (205/55R16 or 225/45R17 all round) can be cross-rotated, Sport-package staggered 225/45R17 front and 255/40R17 rear (wheels 8.5J ET40 vs 9J ET30) can only be swapped side to side if non-directional. No BMW-published rotation interval or pattern was found (forum claims that BMW recommends against rotation are secondhand and not E90-specific). The earlier 'lift at the rear differential' advice is withdrawn: sources conflict, so use the side jack pads.
variantDependencies: DECODED CONFIG: rear-wheel drive (type PH73), S2KU alloy wheels style 285, S2VB tire pressure indicator (direct TPMS, also NHTSA). Tire size and run-flat status are not coded: read the sidewalls. [Decoded from the owner's VIN by one free decoder (bimmer.work option list) on 2026-10-10; an absence of an option code is an inference. Treat as probable and verify at the car.]

VIN WBAPH7C58AA175760 decodes at NHTSA vPIC to BMW 328i, 2010, Sedan, 3.0 L, 230 hp, Munich, TPMS Direct. [https://vpic.nhtsa.dot.gov/api/vehicles/DecodeVinValues/WBAPH7C58AA175760?format=json&modelyear=2010]

RWD vs xDrive: NHTSA returns AWD for the sister pattern WBAPK7C5 and no drive type for this VIN's WBAPH7C5, suggesting RWD. Retailer tire tables (sizemytires, Mavis) list staggered Sport-package fitment on the 328i xDrive as well, so drivetrain does not decide the tire package.
Tire package: square 205/55R16 91H (16 in) or 225/45R17 91H/91V; staggered 17 in Sport package 225/45R17 front, 255/40R17 rear (sizemytires, Mavis, Apex). Read the sidewalls.
Wheel widths: Apex lists 17x8.5 ET40 front and 17x9 ET30 rear for the staggered set, so staggered wheels cannot be swapped front to rear.
Directional tires: stock Potenza RE050A direction is disputed by forum posts; read the sidewall arrow.
TPMS: NHTSA says Direct; Mitchell/Modern Tire Dealer says 2009-13 E90 can be TPM (direct) or FTM (indirect), told apart by metal valve stems.
Spare: a compact spare or snow chains must not be fitted during a TPMS reset (Tomorrow's Technician).
Engine, transmission: no source shows any effect on rotation.

tools.item: 17 mm wheel-bolt socket (1/2 in drive) and breaker bar
Floor jack, rated jack stands, wheel chocks; pad (wood or hockey-puck) between jack and plastic jack pad
Locking-bolt key if fitted (from the wheel-lock set)
Tire pressure gauge and inflator; correct pressures are required before a TPMS reset
Wire brush or cloth to clean hub and wheel mounting faces (general practice, not in an E90 source)
tools.conflicts: Autodoc steps apply copper grease to the rotor-to-wheel contact area, which implies cleaning it first.

parts.item: No parts required for a rotation
Wheel bolts: M12x1.5 thread, 17 mm hex, 60-degree taper seat, 5 per wheel on a 5x120 pattern (replacement only)
parts.note: 5x120 and the bolt (not nut) design come from koleso.ee only; thread and hex from Bimmerworld and tpautorepair.

torque.conflicts: Dissent: koleso.ee wheel database lists 115 Nm with no source. FCP states 119 Nm (88 lb-ft), a rounding of the same figure. Department 69 attributes 120 Nm to BMW TIS (workshop-manuals.com) and says TIS also instructs re-checking all wheel bolts after installation; that TIS page itself could not be fetched, hence primary:false. BimmerWorld's 75 ft-lb applies only to its aftermarket nuts.

torque.value: MISSING (read the placard on the car; EU data in koleso.ee lists 2.2 bar front for 205/55R16, not a US figure)

steps.title: Identify tire package and direction
steps.instruction: Read all four sidewalls. Same size all round (205/55R16 or 225/45R17) is square. Narrower front 225/45R17 and wider rear 255/40R17 is staggered. Note any rotation arrow and any 'inside/outside' marking, plus the tire date code.
warnings: Never swap staggered tires front to rear: the wheels differ in width and offset.

steps.title: Choose the pattern
steps.instruction: Square and non-directional: rearward cross (rears forward on same side, fronts to opposite rear) or front/rear swap. Square directional: swap front and rear on the same side only. Staggered and non-directional: swap left and right on the same axle only (Apex, Velgen); front and rear wheels differ in width and offset so they never trade axles. Staggered and directional: tires would have to be remounted on the opposite wheels (Velgen), so most owners skip rotation. If tires are worn unevenly or you are unsure, have a shop do it.
warnings: No BMW document on rotation was found; forum claims that BMW recommends against rotating are secondhand and not E90-specific.
Forum posts disagree on whether stock RE050A is directional; read the sidewall.

steps.title: Loosen bolts on the ground, then lift and support
steps.instruction: With the car on the ground break each 17 mm bolt loose about one turn, chock a wheel on the other axle, then jack at the plastic jack pads (sill points) and place stands. If using a center jack point, note the conflict: sources describe the rear centre as the differential housing, the crossmember behind it, or not permitted at all, so prefer side jack points with a pad between jack and plastic.
warnings: Stands, not the jack, hold the car.
One forum thread quotes BMW that rear-centre jacking is not allowed on the E90; do not jack on the aluminium diff cover.
xDrive front centre point is reported to differ from RWD (single forum source).

steps.title: Move the wheels
steps.instruction: Remove the bolts while supporting each wheel, move wheels per the chosen pattern, and clean any rust or dirt off the hub face and the wheel mounting face. Note any locking bolt and keep the key at hand.
warnings: Hub-centric fit: keep mounting faces clean so the wheel seats flat (general practice).

steps.title: Refit and torque in a star pattern
steps.instruction: Start every bolt by hand, snug in a crisscross order with the wheel on the stands, lower the car, then torque all five bolts per wheel to 120 Nm in a crisscross sequence.
warnings: Torque is secondary-sourced; do not torque hot bolts.
BMW TIS (per Department 69) says to re-check after installation.

steps.title: Set tire pressures
steps.instruction: Set all four tires to the placard pressures (cold). The placard values for this car are not in a source; read them from the car.
warnings: Do not guess pressures from EU data.

steps.title: Reset the tire pressure monitor
steps.instruction: This car's VIN decodes as direct TPMS. With pressures set and the engine running: iDrive cars use Vehicle Info > Vehicle Status > RESET TPM (Tomorrow's Technician) or Settings > TPM > Reset TPM (Modern Tire Dealer); cars without iDrive scroll the turn-signal stalk to the TPMS RESET/INIT item and hold the button about 5 seconds. Then drive about 15 minutes; the reset resumes if interrupted.
warnings: Do not reset with a compact spare or snow chains fitted.
If metal valve stems are not present the car may be FTM (indirect); the reset menu is the same.

steps.title: Re-check the bolts
steps.instruction: After the first short drive re-check wheel-bolt torque and tire pressures.
warnings: Re-check after a short drive is general practice; BMW TIS 're-check after installation' is attributed by Department 69.

safety: Use rated jack stands on level ground; do not rely on the jack or on the aluminium differential cover.
Do not rotate staggered tires front to rear; do not rotate directional tires across sides without remounting.
Torque wheel bolts to 120 Nm in a crisscross order and re-check after a short drive; value is secondary-sourced.
Do not torque hot bolts; do not use anti-seize/grease on the bolt threads unless BMW says to (no source says to).
Do not reset TPMS with a spare or chains fitted.

visuals.title: Plastic jack pads at the sill

elements.describe: A small rectangular plastic jacking pad on the underside of the sill, one at each of four jack points.
A wood block or cut hockey puck placed between the jack and the plastic pad.

facts.note: Bimmerpost and Bimmerforums: small plastic rectangular blocks at four jack points (BMW part 'Support lifting platform' 51717123311); BimmerWorld sells the pad (E90/E92 fitment list); Turner sells an adapter that fits into the plastic lifting points, listing E90 328i.

Bimmerpost: lift points on the rocker panels; BimmerWorld: the hard block sits on the underside of the rocker panel at the factory jacking point. Bimmerforums loosely says 'on the frame' at the four corners.
One website: wood or hockey-puck pad between jack and pad.

mustNotDepict.reason: Exact distance from wheels and pad dimensions are not established.
Rear-centre and front-centre jack points are in conflict and must not be shown as approved.

https://g42.bimmerpost.com/forums/showth.establishes: Lift points on the rocker panels; hockey pucks as pads.
Plastic rectangular pads at four jack points.
Plastic boxes under the car that the OEM jack fits into; rear-centre jacking said to be disallowed.

https://www.bimmerforums.com/forum/archi.establishes: E90 thread: four jacking points with little plastic blocks; OEM name 'support lifting platform' 51717123311; can crack under a bare floor-jack cup.

https://www.bimmerworld.com/Tools/BMW-Ja.establishes: BMW jack pad 51717164761 sits on the underside of the rocker panel at the jacking point; page text says E92 coupe but fitment list includes E90.

visuals.title: Wheel bolts, locking bolt and the metal TPMS valve stem

elements.describe: Five hex-head wheel bolts per wheel on a 5-lug circle, tightened in a crisscross order.
One bolt per wheel that needs a special key, if the car has a lock set.
A metal tire valve stem, which indicates a direct TPMS sensor inside the tire.

facts.note: 3 sites: 17 mm hex, M12x1.5, taper seat.
1 site: 5x120 pattern, so five bolts; no second site.

RealOEM for this car lists 'Wheel bolt lock with adaptor' / 'Set wheel locks' (M12x1.5, 17 mm adaptor) as an option/accessory; TP Auto Repair says cars with anti-theft locking bolts need a dedicated key. Not confirmed fitted on this VIN.
Modern Tire Dealer says the metal stem is the only external clue; Tomorrow's Technician says direct systems use valve-stem sensors; NHTSA says this VIN has direct TPMS. 3 sites.
RealOEM: wheel bolt M12x1.5 quantity 20 per car (5 per wheel); Koleso: lug bolts, 5x120; TP Auto Repair: BMW wheels use bolts threading into the hub.
Five bolts per wheel on a 5x120 bolt circle through the wheel face into the hub.
RealOEM lists a screw-in RDC valve and RDC valve cap per wheel (from 03/2007); Tomorrow's Technician says the sensor is mounted in the valve stem on the wheel rim.

mustNotDepict.reason: Not confirmed as fitted; key pattern shape not established.
Wheel spoke design and finish are unknown for this car.

visuals.title: TPMS reset: iDrive menu and turn-signal stalk

elements.describe: The end button of the turn-signal stalk, used to scroll to TPMS RESET and hold for about 5 seconds.
An on-screen menu (Vehicle Info > Vehicle Status, or Settings > TPM) with a RESET TPM item.

facts.note: 2 sites: scroll with the stalk to RESET/INIT and hold about 5 seconds, then drive.
2 sites, but menu names differ (Vehicle Status > RESET TPM vs Settings > TPM > Reset TPM).
All three describe resetting TPM with a scroll switch and a button on the turn-signal stalk (hold about 5 s).
Import Car (2009-2011 3-Series): push the button on the end of the turn-signal stalk; Modern Tire Dealer: button on the turn-indicator lever. Stalk is the left-hand column lever.
iDrive cars have a RESET TPM item; menu path wording differs.
Tomorrow's Technician and Import Car: Vehicle Info > Vehicle Status > RESET TPM; Modern Tire Dealer (Mitchell): Settings > TPM > reset.

mustNotDepict.reason: Exact on-screen layout and menu wording are not consistent across sources.
Stalk shape and button position are not described.

https://www.tomorrowstechnician.com/bmw-.establishes: 2009-11 3-series stalk reset (hold ~5 s, drive 15 min); iDrive Vehicle Status RESET TPM.

https://www.import-car.com/tpms-update-b.establishes: 2009-2011 3-Series: scroll stalk switch to TPMS RESET, press end-of-stalk button, hold ~5 s; iDrive path Vehicle Info > Vehicle Status > RESET TPM.
